items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: I sent for Emmanuel Perez, Lorenzo Teal, Louis Cottrell, and I brought an outfit here to work for Mike Fritzel... And I put them in the Ansonia for Mike.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Just a little before the war. Because just about that time, I went, I was playing at the Washington Theater here, 31st and State. And I sent for Emmanuel Perez, Lorenzo Teal, Louis Cottrell, and I brought an outfit here to work for Mike Fritzel. Yes. At that time, Mike Fritzel had a place on Madison and Paulina. Was that the Ansonia? The Ansonia, that's right. And I put them in the Ansonia for Mike. And I had intended, as the orchestra developed, I had intended to take the move over with me. But they were…
Excuse me for interrupting your train of thought, but is Mike Fritzel still here, you think? No, Mike died.

items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: Another father he played with was Charles Elgar. I knew him.

ctx.x: No, no. Another father he played with was Charles Elgar. I knew him. He's still up there. He's an officer in the union. He's vice president. He's vice president. Many years. They were just about the same age. My father might be one or two years older than he. A fellow by the name of Ralph Marniegu. That was another one in that old brass band in that area. Ralph Marniegu. That was a soldier. Who I saw. I heard him mention out. I said Crusto. That's the name. Diddy Chandler. Diddy Chandler came up right around in…

Oh yes. We never didn't know much about Mac Murray. You happen to know what his real name... Some people say his first name was Mac and his last name Murray? No, that was his last name. His last name was Mac Murray. Now, I'm trying to think what was his first name.
